The Director-General of the National Institute for Sports, Philip Shaibu, has urged the Super Eagles not to give up on qualifying for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations, insisting that the team’s hopes remain alive despite the goalless draw against Tanzania. Shaibu spoke after watching Tuesday’s 0-0 draw in Zanzibar, which left Nigeria with seven points from four Group L games, three behind leaders Guinea-Bissau, who beat Madagascar 2-0. Tanzania have already qualified as co-hosts, so only one ticket remains in the group. In a statement issued by the NIS on Shaibu’s message to supporters and football stakeholders, he said the race was far from over. He pointed to the Matchday Five and Six fixtures in March 2027, when Nigeria travel to Madagascar on March 24 and host Guinea-Bissau four days later. He asked the Super Eagles to draw inspiration from the Flamingos, who recovered from an opening-day defeat at the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco to progress in the competition, and to show the same resilience and determination. Shaibu also recalled the qualifying campaign for the 2010 World Cup in South Africa. Nigeria appeared to be trailing Tunisia for the group’s only ticket, but Tunisia lost on the final day while the Eagles beat Kenya to qualify. He said such examples should motivate the current squad. Morocco matches Nigeria’s No.5 best FIFA rankings CMFC partners Tanzanian firm on gold project FIFA ranking: Super Eagles rise one place to 29th globally He cautioned the technical crew and players against taking the expectations of millions of Nigerians for granted, and stressed the importance of the team to the nation’s sporting identity and pride. He wished the team an injury-free run ahead of the decisive games. Nigeria could still revive their campaign with wins over Madagascar and Guinea-Bissau. A strong performance, along with the required goal difference, could see them overtake Guinea-Bissau and take the group’s sole ticket to the 2027 AFCON, which is co-hosted by Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda. Head coach Eric Chelle admitted after the draw that Nigeria were in trouble. “A draw away from home is not a bad result, but in our situation, because we lost to Guinea-Bissau, that is why we are in trouble,” he said.
